non_blocking_notes: Provenance-issue de-duplication in _merge_provider_issues (discovery.py) is never exercised: every test provider gets license and citation set via the replace() in the recording_stages fixture, so the legacy handle never appends provenance.license_not_established / provenance.citation_not_established, and every test asserts result.issues == (). A regression that dropped provenance issues entirely, or that stopped de-duplicating them, would pass the whole suite. A single fixture variant with license=None/citation=None asserting exactly one copy of each provenance issue plus one warning would close this.

_merge_provider_issues classifies provider-level issues by the string prefix issue.code.startswith("provenance.") rather than an explicit code set. It matches the two codes the plan names, but it silently widens de-duplication to any future provenance.* code, including a per-series one that should be retained twice. An explicit frozenset of provider-level codes would state the intent the docstring implies.

Three defensive FatalContractError branches added in this change are unreachable under the current invariants and untested: the reason is None branch in fetch() (needed only for type narrowing, since the selection invariant guarantees a concrete _EmptyReason), the empty-results branch in _merge_provider_results, and the missing start/end request-key branch. They are harmless, but they are the only lines in the new production code with no coverage.

The provider-scoped merge keeps the first per-series result's requested_at, so the merged provenance timestamps the first request rather than the call. That follows the plan's "use the first result's provenance as the base" instruction and is correct for this step; it is worth noting in case a later milestone wants a call-level requested_at.

tests/test_fetch.py::test_fetch_functions_require_rivretrieve_selection_and_defer_request_controls takes recording_stages only to delete it (del recording_stages). The fixture is genuinely needed (it disables default provider registration), but the del reads as dead code; a comment or a rename would make the dependency legible.
summary:
PR #136 delivers the m4-s1 contract as written and should land. Verified against the named refs, not the working tree.

Contract conformance: fetch() calls _require_selection first, then raises EmptySelectionError with error.reason IS selection.empty_reason and the exact plan message, then partitions by provider and raises MultiProviderSelectionError naming both providers and directing to fetch_by_provider — both guards run before _provider_lookup, and the tests assert provider_lookups == [] and both recording stages' calls == [], so the atomicity claim is checked at the seam, not merely asserted. Routing is exactly per-series: for the sparse selection the recorded stage calls are [(('station-1',),('level',)), (('station-2',),('level_hourly',))], which a Cartesian regression would fail. fetch_by_provider returns an insertion-ordered dict in sorted provider order, never merges across providers, and its per-provider results are asserted to have singular provenance.provider_id/license/citation, a provider-scoped RawPayload identity, the exact four model_fields, the five ADR-0006 columns in order, and no provider_id column. The empty selection returns {} with zero lookups and zero stage calls. The zone-refusal test confirms ADR-0016 rejection still happens before stage fetch through the new route.

Fences held: raw= and on_issue= are absent from both public signatures (asserted by inspect.signature) and RawMode's fate is untouched — the new route pins raw=RawMode.OMIT, on_issue="ignore" internally and applies apply_on_issue(..., "warn") once to the merged result, matching the existing registry.py pattern. No legacy public name was deleted or modified; src/rivretrieve/__init__.py adds exactly the two re-exports and __version__ stays "0.1.49". The only pre-existing assertion changed is test_package.py's public-name set, which gains exactly "fetch" and "fetch_by_provider" (17 names); nothing was weakened, skipped, or xfailed, and no noqa or type-ignore was added. Write-set is exactly the four planned paths, one commit, commit message is the exact subject with no trailers or attribution footer, and pr-body.md is untracked.

Measured myself at 26f91ca: uv run pytest -> 1649 passed, 2 skipped (baseline 1643 + the 6 new tests; the only skips are the two pre-existing missing-folium skips at tests/test_map_stations.py:179 and :190). uv run ty check src -> All checks passed. uv run ruff format --check -> 167 files already formatted. uv run ruff check -> All checks passed. Per instructions I did not run uv build. The PR body's four summary bullets each correspond to code I read in the diff. Worktree left tracked-clean (git status --short shows only ?? pr-body.md).

The residual observations are coverage and legibility, not defects — chiefly that the provenance-issue de-duplication branch is dead in the test suite because every fixture provider has a license and citation. That is a gap a follow-up should close, not a reason to hold this merge.
